o1.biggest_strength: Clean, shootable scripts built on the real data: taste-first openers, the 3 pm hook, price handled head-on, disclosure written into every brief.
o1.biggest_mistake: Script 3's hook leads on the kids line while the label moment sits mid-script; also the disclosure instruction ('start the caption with #ad') is thinner than platform toggles need, and the briefs are good but a shade wordier than they need to be.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten script 3 so the label is not the spine of a family ad, add the on-screen 'Ad' frame rule and delivered-asset specs (captions, safe zones, raw clips) from the other version, and give each hook a one-word note on what single thing it changes.

o2.biggest_strength: Reads like a producer's plan: opening-style table with cost per purchase, price math on screen, a real test budget with cut rules, and the strongest creator briefs and delivery specs of the two.
o2.biggest_mistake: The spoken disclosure lines ('Olipop paid me for this one', 'Olipop paid me to make this') are clunky and repeated mid-ad; the on-screen 'Ad' from frame one plus the toggle is the compliant part, and the extra spoken plugs hurt the voice. Script 1 also puts a claim before the full reveal rhythm settles.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Drop the awkward spoken payment lines to a single natural mention early, keep the on-screen Ad and toggles, and rewrite script 3 so the dad's line is an observation after the kids' reaction rather than a claim lead-in.

reason: Both are shootable and on-data, but number 2's cost-per-purchase table, on-screen price math, budget test plan and delivery specs are the things I would actually hand to a creator tomorrow; number 1 is the cleaner read but asks me to fill in more of the production detail myself.
